whatItDoes: Plans a path to a savings goal. Enter the target amount, current savings, the monthly contribution, and an expected return rate, and see the required monthly saving, the estimated time to goal, and whether you are on track.
whyItExists: Goals without a number tend to slip by. The math behind reaching a target by a set date is non-trivial, and knowing both the required monthly amount and the projected finish date turns a fuzzy wish into a concrete, trackable plan.
whoShouldUse: Households budgeting for a deposit, emergency-fund builders, big-ticket savers, and financial planners setting milestones.
useCases: Decide how much to save monthly to reach a deposit goal
Set an emergency fund target and the timeline to it
Plan a large upcoming spending like a down payment or wedding
Check whether the current contribution rate is on target
Reverse-engineer a monthly amount from a target date
Model how a return rate accelerates reaching the goal
instructions: Enter the goal amount you want to reach
Enter what you already have saved
Enter the monthly amount you can contribute
Set the expected annual return rate
Read the required monthly amount and the projected time to goal
Adjust any input to see how it changes the plan
examples: Goal $50,000, savings $5,000, $1,000/month, no return → done in about 45 months
Goal $100,000, savings $10,000, 6% return → under $1,300/month needed for 5 years
Goal $20,000 in 2 years with current $2,000 → about $750/month at 0% return
Goal $30,000 in 3 years with $0 saved and 5% return → roughly $765/month required
bestPractices: Break large goals into yearly and monthly targets
Automate your contribution the same day you get paid
Adjust the plan whenever your income or goal changes
Keep an emergency cushion in a separately liquid account
Revisit the plan quarterly to stay honest about progress
commonMistakes: Assuming returns guaranteed and ignoring inflation
Setting a single month of contribution and then never adjusting
Underestimating how long compound growth needs to work
Planning to rely on the goal amount before it's actually earned
Forgetting that a 0% return goal needs every dollar saved manually
faq: Does this tool support multiple currencies? — Yes, select your currency from the dropdown. All calculations run locally in your browser.
What if I can't reach the required monthly amount? — Lengthen the horizon or shrink the goal; the tool lets you see what each choice does.
Does the projection account for inflation? — No, adjust the goal for inflation to model real purchase power.
Can I use a rate of zero? — Yes, that models a no-return cash account.
Is my data private? — Yes, everything runs locally in the browser.
Should I include returns in my plan? — For long goals yes, but use a conservative rate so you're not disappointed.
What is a good emergency fund size? — A common rule of thumb is 3-6 months of essential expenses, saved in a liquid account.
features: Required monthly sum and finish date
Works with or without an assumed return
Goal timeline planning in one view
assumptions: Generic savings goal calculation with compound interest; no country-specific assumptions.
